title: Frontier Anchoring: OKR‑anchored Cost & Latency Prioritization Framework
creator: Arielle Kim
description:
Problem: Existing RICE-derived scores at Redwood often over-index on reach and nominal effort while underweighting operational economics (latency/cost) and alignment to quarterly OKRs. We need a lightweight, repeatable rubric that surfaces: (1) OKR alignment and minimum acceptable performance thresholds, (2) marginal cost/latency elasticity for the feature under realistic traffic shapes, and (3) developer effort and rollout risk.

Proposal: "Frontier Anchoring (FA)" — construct an Opportunity Frontier for each candidate initiative by plotting 'Objective Alignment' (OKR score 0-10) on the X axis and 'Net Unit Cost Delta per 1k requests' adjusted by 95th percentile latency sensitivity on the Y axis. Anchor the frontier with the current OKR threshold (OKR anchor) and an SLO anchor (latency/cost acceptable boundary). Compute a composite 'Frontier Score' that rewards high OKR alignment above the anchor and penalizes movement toward higher cost/latency. The score supplements RICE: we continue to capture Reach and Effort but replace 'Impact' with the Frontier Score to better reflect product & operational priorities.

Why different: Rather than a single scalar impact estimate, FA exposes the trade space as a frontier so PMs and Eng can see non-dominated candidates and choose based on explicit OKR and SLO anchors. It reduces over-prioritization of seemingly high-impact work that would materially increase serving cost or violate latency SLOs.

Intended consumers: PM leads, Eng managers, Platform/Infra stakeholders, Executive roadmap review.
acceptance_criteria: Framework documented with worked example for three feature candidates (chat-caching, adaptive-batching, new model onboarding)
Calculation spreadsheet and Python notebook available that converts perf benchmarks and cost estimates into Frontier Scores
Playbook section added to roadmap review template describing how to set OKR and SLO anchors
At least two upcoming roadmap decisions (Q2 scope) apply FA scoring and include trade-off discussion in PRD

2026-03-02: Platform recommended using 95th percentile latency sensitivity; accepted to penalize tail-latency increases
2026-03-04: Engineering requested an elasticity damping factor for features with high uncertainty; agreed on conservative default (0.6) and flagging for re-eval
2026-03-08: Decided to keep RICE's Reach and Effort as auxiliary columns (for transparency) rather than discard existing metrics
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Initial whiteboard session with PM, Platform, and Runtime teams — sketched frontier concept and anchors

2026-03-06: Reviewed with Eng Leads; requested adding uncertainty flags and a recommended rollout guardrail for any candidate that moves past SLO anchor
